name: starting architecture
last_analysis: All nine trials scored 0 on dev and also 0 on training success. That held across recipes (1 to 4 epochs, gamma 0.9 to 0.99, 98k to 405k steps) and across architectures (footprint-pooling head, per-layer logsumexp, conv head with mask inputs, transformer). Seed noise cannot explain this. Even the easy designs with no overhangs, which a greedy 1x1 policy could build, were never built exactly, even with exploration during training. Something structural is wrong. Since the world "may not behave as described", the most likely cause is that action indices do not map to grid cells as the spec states. The axes might be transposed or flipped, the anchor might differ, or DONE might sit at a different index. Every head so far assumed spatial alignment between feature cells and action indices; a 3x3 conv can absorb a one-cell shift but not a transpose. Final round: dense action heads that learn any index-to-cell mapping, including where DONE is.
